{{Cleanup|referencing cleanup}}
{{Quote|Galaxy upon galaxy. Vast, unexplored realms of space. It is a wild, untamed universe we live in.|[[Mungo Baobab]]|<ref name="Treasure">''[[Treasure of the Hidden Planet]]''</ref>}}
The '''Universe''', sometimes called the '''Known Universe''', was the [[Realspace/Legends|space]] in which many galaxies&mdash;including the [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy]], [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and its companion galaxies&mdash;developed and existed.

==History==
===Formation and composition===
{{Quote|Not just our galaxy but indeed our entire universe may be a Celestial construct.|Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]] on his belief about the universe's creation|<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>}}
The universe was created with the [[Big Bang]]<ref name="SW87">[[Star Wars (1977) 87|''Star Wars'' (1977) 87]]</ref> some time before [[13,000,000,000 BBY]]. Estimates by residents of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] believed that their [[Galaxy/Legends|home]] was formed in that [[Standard year/Legends|year]] from debris in the universe. An enormous cloud of dust and gas experienced a [[Gravity/Legends|gravitic]] collapse to form their disk, one-hundred-thousand lightyears in diameter, with a [[Black hole/Legends|black hole]] at the center that its contents [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]]. The galaxy contained approximately four-hundred-billion [[Star/Legends|stars]].<ref name="EGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], p. x.</ref><ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Several companion galaxies formed as well and began orbiting the galaxy.
[[File:Galaxy1.png|right|thumb|The galaxy and a glimpse of a tiny part of the universe, from outside the galaxy.]]
Other galaxies were created as well. In [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|another]] that developed its own star systems, a planet, later known as [[Yuuzhan'tar]], would develop the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] and a vast number of other sentient species.

Though little evidence backed it up, some scientists, such as Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]] believed that the entire universe was possibly built by the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===The Force===
{{Quote|Well, the Force is what gives a Jedi his power. It's an energy field created by all living things. It surrounds us and penetrates us; it binds the galaxy together.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]|audio=theforce.flac|<ref name="IFYLOFD">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
Holding together the universe was [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], a fundamental power that penetrated and connected all things within it.<ref name="POD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> It interacted with the life in the galaxy through semi-sentient micro-organisms called [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> For a long while, the Force was a subject of philosophy, an abstract concept independently studied by a number of groups across the galaxy, technology not yet advanced enough for them to collaborate.<ref name="Atlas" /> Their early rationalization of the Force consisted of two opposing entities: all the goodness and compassion in the universe, called [[Light side of the Force/Legends|Ashla]]; and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Bogan]], representing all unhindered, passionate emotion.<ref name="ROE">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>

Over eons, individuals in groups splintered from this one order continued contemplating the reality of the Force and what it meant in isolation. Eventually, they came to the resolution that the Force and the powers were meant to be used in the pursuit of social responsibility and the isolationist mentality was abandoned in favor of spreading the benefits of the Force into the wider galaxy.<ref name="I novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> Certain individuals, like [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Dyer/Legends|Dyer]]<ref name="Card-CCG-Colonel Dyer">{{CCG|set=Endor Limited|cardname=Colonel Dyer}}</ref> were merely [[Force-attunement|Force-attuned]], connected to the Force but not able to utilize any powers.<ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref>

[[File:Lightsiders_btm.jpg|right|thumb|Famous practictioners of the light side.]]
Nonetheless, there was more to mystical power than Ashla, also called the "light side of the Force," and Bogan, also called the "dark side." [[Caleb]], a healer, drew power and wisdom directly from the universe.<ref name="DOE" /> When his contemporary [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], felt his power, he registered it as the Force, but not exactly. In essence, Bane felt it was more like nature itself. This power allowed him to greatly increase his fortitude, and to show Bane this he dipped his hand into a boiling potion without flinching.<ref name="POD" />

Over the eons, many Force users would feel that the use of the Force put them in touch with the universe as a whole;<ref name="Crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref><ref name="Rogue Planet">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref> otherwise, its use would make them perceive the entire universe as responding to them in some way. When a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] experienced a [[Force vision/Legends|vision of possible futures]], it could seem like the passage of time in the entire universe slowed for the person while they took in the information.<ref name="Deceived">''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''</ref><ref name="The Old Republic: Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> When using [[Psychometry/Legends|psychometry]], a [[Force power/Legends|Force power]] that allowed one to read impressions from objects, one felt as though they could distinctly feel the object's place in the universe.<ref name="FA">''[[The Old Republic: Fatal Alliance]]''</ref>

[[File:Darksiders_btm.jpg|left|thumb|Famous practictioners of the dark side.]]
The Jedi, who believed using the light side of the Force should be preferred over the dark side, and Sith, who felt the opposite. These groups clashed in the galaxy for thousands of years, and the Jedi believed that the use of the dark side corrupted the Sith and made them evil. From the Sith point of view, they used the Force as a tool and embraced life and the Jedi led restricted, weak lives in service of the Force, as dictated by the Jedi Council.<ref name="K2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> At one point, a sect of Jedi apprentices theorized that the Force was neither good nor evil, and that the Force, which they rechristened "the [[Potentium]]," was universally good: a wholly positive field that permeated the universe while instructing its inhabitants to do good. They believed that connection with the Potentium should not be diluted through training or learning in one aspect of it, shunning others. With this in mind, they felt that it was impossible for the Potentium to sway someone to commit evil acts, for there was no innate malevolence in the Potentium and it could never ask that of a Force user. Followers of the Potentium philosophy were [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] from the Jedi Order for their heretical beliefs.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

Generations of Padawans under the original Jedi Order would be warned against falling into the Potentium's way of thinking,<ref name="Rogue Planet" /> and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who founded and led the succeeding [[New Jedi Order]], also shunned the spirit of the principle. He taught that to view the two sides of the Force as tools, interchangeable for different situations, was to try inapproriately to twist the nature of the Force to someone's will and that it would cause Jedi to fall to the dark side once tempted to use it regularly.<ref name="Tat3">[[Legacy (2006) 39|''Legacy'' (2006) 39]]</ref>

===The galaxy imperils the universe===
{{Quote|Our ancestor believed that out of the universal armageddon of a new, artificially-generated Big Bang might come with a better tomorrow&hellip; Lucky for all he never became quite depressed enough to use his device, and its secrets were lost with his death&hellip;|[[Santor]]|<ref name="SW87" />}}
[[File:Shawkenese_universe_destroyer_screen.jpg|right|thumb|Simulation of the Shawkenese universe destroying weapon.]]
At some point, a nihilistic [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Shawken]] created the [[Shawken Device]], a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] designed to re-trigger the Big Bang and create a new universe. He believed this was the only way to give existence purpose, though he never reached a level of despair that would have prompted him to use it and he never told anyone how it worked. It was buried in the planet and remained there for a very long time.<ref name="SW87" />

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Shawken Device was unearthed by [[Rik Duel/Legends|Rik Duel]] and his gang. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Kiro]] found the gang and defeated them, deactivating the device. It was never clear to anyone if it would have actually worked.<ref name="SW87" />

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], [[Hethrir]] bridged the gap between the universe and a [[Waru's universe|universe in an alternate dimension]], from which he brought an entity known as [[Waru]] into his own.<ref name="Waru">''[[The Crystal Star]]''</ref>

==History in metaphor==
{{Quote|Statistically speaking, the universe is empty. But at faster-than-light speeds, it fills up very quickly.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Pers Pradeux]], demonstrating the penchant for referring to the galaxy as "the universe"|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
To illustrate metaphorically the importance<ref name="KE4">[[Knight Errant 4|''Knight Errant'' 4]]</ref><ref name="IFYLOFD" /><ref name="Smuggler Van">{{SWArchive|url=games/videgames/tor_smugglersvanguard/index.html|text=''The Old Republic: Smuggler's Vanguard''|int=The Old Republic: Smuggler's Vanguard}}</ref><ref name="Cloak of Deception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref><ref name="Podrace to Freedom">''[[Episode I Adventures 14: Podrace to Freedom]]''</ref> or insignificance<ref name="Deceived" /><ref name="FA" /><ref name="Anakin Journal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref><ref name="II novel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref> of an object,<ref name="FA" /><ref name="IFYLOFD" /> a situation,<ref name="I novel" /><ref name="Rogue Planet" /><ref name="FA" /><ref name="Smuggler Van" /> themselves,<ref name="Rogue Planet" /><ref name="Deceived" /><ref name="KE4" /><ref name="II novel" /> or others,<ref name="I novel" /><ref name="Rogue Planet" /><ref name="Anakin Journal" /> people would examine whatever it was in relation to the universe. Color-commentator Fode of [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fodesinbeed Annodue]] once joked about the existence of multiple universes to emphasize the pain a [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|Podracer]] pilot would feel if they crashed their [[Podracer/Legends|craft]], asserting that it would hurt for a denizen of any of them.<ref name="TPM" /> Before the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Jaled Dur]] created the [[Heart of the Universe]], a gem that augmented Force powers.<ref name="Star Wars Gamemaster Screen">''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Screen]]''</ref> [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] believed that the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|DS-1 Orbital Battle Station]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] was the most powerful instrument of death in the universe.<ref name="IFYLOFD" />

It was also possible to describe someone possessing a vastly different view of life than the speaker as in their own universe. For instance, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] from the planet of [[Stewjon/Legends|Stewjon]],<ref name="Twitter Q&A">{{Twitter|starwars|status/21159260939|[[StarWars.com]]|archivedate=20190801103354}}</ref> thought of [[Roper Slam]] as in his own universe, as the latter was a gangster far removed from the Jedi and their refined lifestyle.<ref name="Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard">''[[Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard]]''</ref>

There was also the idea that even individual people and small acts could affect change in the grander scheme. [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]], a slave on the planet of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], once told her son, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], that every act of kindness slightly assuaged the problems of the universe. However, Anakin felt there was far too much strife for him to do anything about it easily. Shmi told him to make a habit of trying anyway.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 5: The Ghostling Children">''[[Episode I Adventures 5: The Ghostling Children]]''</ref> The biggest of the universe's problems, she believed, was that no-one helped anyone else, and she dedicated herself to working against this by finding ways to aid whoever was in need.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine">''[[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine]]''</ref>

In addition, individuals from the galaxy tended to have a view of existence centered around their own galaxy. They referred to the galaxy as "the universe" on a number of occasions.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" /><ref name="Rising Force">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Rising Force]]''</ref> This semantic centralism pervaded galactic society to the point that the planet of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] was thought of by almost every civilized person there as the center of the universe.<ref name="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> This was also qualified as "the center of the Known Universe,"<ref name="BobaFettFight">''[[Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive]]''</ref> and the Jedi considered their [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Temple]] on that world the center of civilized society in the Known Universe.<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

The word ''universal'' and its derivatives were used to describe things as all encompassing.<ref name="II novel" /><ref name="TAS">''[[The Approaching Storm]]''</ref><ref name="TSSS">''[[Star Wars Adventures 5: The Shape-Shifter Strikes]]''</ref>

===The face of the universe===
{{Quote|The weak will always be victims. That is the way of the universe. The strong take what they want, and the weak suffer at their hands. That is their fate; it is inevitable. Only the strong survive, because only the strong deserve to.''"<br />"''You only believe that because you don't know what it's like to suffer!''"<br />"''I know what it means to suffer. I used to be a victim. But I refused to accept my lot in life. I made myself strong. Those who are victims have no one to blame but themselves. They do not deserve pity; they are victims because of their own failures and weaknesses.|Darth Bane and [[Serra]]|<ref name="DOE" />}}
In reference to the natural state of things, however they interpreted it, people would say that it was the way the universe worked.<ref name="FA" /><ref name="DOE" /> [[Darth Chratis]], a Sith who served the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] during the [[Great Galactic War]], tried to convince [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Shigar Konshi]] to become his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] by explaining why the Sith killed others. He told Konshi of his Empire's subjects that lived in hatred of the Jedi because they had killed similarly as a means to stop the Sith: taking the lives of those peoples' family and friends. He believed that killing was not to be shied away from because it was how to gain the upper hand over others and that that was the way the universe worked: strength was honed by conflicts, a person or group pitted against an enemy and overcoming them.<ref name="FA" />

A similar doctrine would also be followed by the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Banite Sith]] in their practice of the [[Code of the Sith/Legends|Code of the Sith]]. Darth Zannah learned from her Master that that life was defined by conflict and that it took strength to survive. People who could not endure their strife, or became complacent, were snuffed out soon enough and it was their own fault. In the practice of the dark side, they saw this idea as crucial: the reason there were those who followed the dark path and regretted it for the damage it did to their lives was that they were too weak to control themselves in their pursuits. Those people were not fit to use the dark side to shape their world and ascend to true freedom and self-reliance, dominating the wills of those around them.<ref name="DOE" />

[[Caleb]], Serra's father<ref name="DOE" /> who had been killed by Zannah,<ref name="ROE" /> saw the opposite as the truth: that instead of asserting dominance, the strong should help the weak be strong as well.<ref name="DOE" /> Caleb was a healer from the planet of [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], where he helped those in need, though not Jedi or Sith.<ref name="POD" /> He followed neither the light side of the Force or the dark side, not wanting to support either, and found power in the universe that one could draw on for wisdom and strength.<ref name="DOE" /> When Bane encountered the man, he found that Caleb's will was augmented not by the Force, in a strict sense, but instead his inner power was derived from nature.<ref name="POD" /> He instilled his ideals and this practice into his daughter, warning her against giving into the dark side that he perceived as evil. Serra once tried to debate with Bane on this point after her [[Marriage/Legends|husband]], [[Gerran]], was killed many years later, which spurred her to seek out her father's killer and exact her revenge&mdash;she was convinced that Bane had murdered him. She found that Bane, whom she had captured and was [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] to avenge her loved ones, threw her points back at her saying that Caleb's philosophy was why her father had been killed. When she told him that she wanted him to know what being victimized felt like, he said that he already had experienced that and had overcome it to make himself stronger, using that to validate his view. Moreover, he stated that had he been stronger, more cautious, he would not have let himself be captured by the princess in the first place. When he escaped, he resolved to kill Serra in order to overcome that show of weakness.<ref name="DOE" />

On Serra's side, fearing for her life, she came to a resolution that her father's universal interpretation was correct and that it was abandoning her father's teachings that had brought her to where she was. Instead of coming to terms with what had happened to her, she gave in to her desires for penance, which lead to a series of decisions made in this pursuit that culminated ultimately in her death at the hands of Bane's second apprentice, [[Darth Cognus]], who was introduced to the Dark Lord because of Serra's actions.<ref name="DOE" />

Still, though many Force users contemplated the universe with its relationship to the Force in mind,<ref name="DOE" /> there was a division between knowing the spiritual ways of the Force and the ways of the universe. When faced with reality by venturing out from his studies at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, Obi-Wan Kenobi realized he had lived a sheltered life and was appalled by the depravity and greed he witnessed from a [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]] named [[Jemba]]. This was enough for him to question momentarily his future as a Jedi, a servant of the Force, wondering if despite his conditioning he was still capable of unsavory acts, a person in the universe who wanted Jemba to pay for his actions with his life.<ref name="Rising Force" /> Jedi were notorious for their reluctance to follow military orders when these conflicted with their creed.<ref name="Annihilation">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]''</ref>

Hylo Visz believed that if someone lost faith in their abilities, they would not be able to progress at all.<ref name="Smuggler Van" />

A young [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], new to [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]], once observed the underside of a [[Tibanna/Legends|Tibanna]] [[Tibannopolis|mining settlement]] on the planet of [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] and took note of the predatory hierarchy observed by the plants and animals living there. Fett saw this as an example of how harsh the universe could be, and he resolved to be like [[Jango Fett/Legends|his father]] and be tough as well.<ref name="Cross">''[[Boba Fett: Crossfire]]''</ref>

===Sentience and the will of the Force===
{{Quote|Difficult to see. Always in motion is the future.|Yoda|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
Some would muse that the universe, sometimes the galaxy,<ref name="Tat3" /> was sentient, actively affecting their situations,<ref name="FA" /><ref name="Smuggler Van" /><ref name="RH">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref> or, more generally, in a destiny they were meant to fulfill.<ref name="Tat3" /><ref name="Podrace to Freedom" /><ref name="Mon1">[[Legacy (2006) 43|''Legacy'' (2006) 43]]</ref> Force users like [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] believed this was done through the Force, which Force-sensitives were able to use to have visions of the future. Jedi like [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] advised caution in their interpretation because the future was always changing.<ref name="ESB" /> Darth Sidious, believing in the Force believed that if one was inelegant in anticipating events this way, their chances at their most advantageous foreseen outcome would be dashed instantly and irrevocably.<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> In this vein, many things people dismissed as happenstance would be interpreted as the will of the Force by Sith or Jedi. [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], believed that this aided him in his search for Sith artifacts: there was a natural cycle to the strength of the dark side and the power of the Sith. Sith artifacts tended to be lost when they weakened. When they increased, Bane could sense, manipulate, and take advantage of this to successfully seek such objects out.<ref name="DOE" /> There was credence to these precognitive beliefs, as shown in the truth of such visions,<ref name="ESB" /> but the correlation was actually stronger than most were able to perceive. It was the Force user who was unable to read the future properly. [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]] achieved extraordinarily accurate predictions because he had a biological advantage over other Sith and Jedi: he was of the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] species. The cognitive abilities of his species were unmatched in the galaxy and he used that in tandem with his skills as a master mathematician to calculate the future quantitatively.<ref name="The Tenebrous Way">{{InsiderCite|130|The Tenebrous Way}}</ref> Even when it did not involve visions of the future, if a Force-user sensed something or received another kind of signal, they would interpret it as the Force attempting to guide them.<ref name="Mon1" />

When in severely dire straights, people would think the universe was out to get them,<ref name="RH" /><ref name="Jedi Apprentice: The Evil Experiment">''[[Jedi Apprentice: The Evil Experiment]]''</ref> sometimes thinking it demonstrated a sense of humor in its execution.<ref name="FA" /><ref name="DP" /> Nonetheless, good influences were registered as well.<ref name="Smuggler Van" /> Still others, like the [[Prince/Legends|princess]] [[Serra]], thought that the universe was completely random, albeit cruel.<ref name="DOE" />

Luke Skywalker and his [[Jedi High Council (New Jedi Order)|Jedi High Council]] believed that the blossoming love between his son, [[Ben Skywalker]], and a Sith named [[Vestara Khai]] may have been the will of the Force.<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>

===Sentiments of universal granduer===
====Invisible Law of the Universe====
An example of someone believing the universe could benefit people with its supposed sentience, the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Hylo Visz]] believed that small instances of bad luck were harbingers of greater misfortune. These were warnings directly from the universe while good signs foreshadowed positive events. She termed this the [[Invisible Law of the Universe]] and was convinced of its validity by events like [[Hylo Visz's father|her father's]] [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] breaking down the day before his [[Battle of Balmorra (Galactic Wars)|death]]. She believed that if she was not having bad luck, she was not in danger and felt she could perform any feat she liked without being harmed if she maintained faith in herself while being wary of messages stemming from the Invisible Law.<ref name="Smuggler Van" />

====Sith brothers====
{{Quote|I was bored&mdash;and so I created the universe. I have no direct knowledge of the time before time. But I infer that wherever I was, nothing could challenge me. And so I created a new existence. All matter, all energy are manifestations of my undying spirit. But while I gave all beings motion, not all beings serve me. For I also created an opponent -- in Odion. He claims he is my older brother -- But I, of course, have no kin or kind. He is simply what I must overcome to advance.|Daiman|<ref name="KE4" />}}
The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Daiman]] was born in [[1057 BBY]]<ref name="Birth">Page 35 of the [[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'' novel]] mentions that Daiman was born 25 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of the book. As the [[StarWars.com]] article [http://www.starwars.com/vault/books/knight_errant_lego/index.html Engineering with LEGOs: Creating the Ships of ''Knight Errant''] states that Knight Errant is set in [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]], this places Daiman's birth in 1057 BBY.</ref> and grew to believe that he was the Creator of the Universe because he was bored in his former existence and wanted a challenge, so he created a new one and all within it. Everything in creation was, as extensions of his spirit made manifest, insignificant compared to him.<ref name="KE4" /> Every action anyone took, in his view, was either a move for his benefit or one to undermine his absolute authority.<ref name="Knight Errant: Aflame 2">[[Knight Errant 2|''Knight Errant'' 2]]</ref> On the other hand, his brother, [[Odion]], believed that his own purpose was to destroy as much as possible, though he focused on the galaxy instead of the whole universe. All people existed to be killed by him.

====''Daen nosi''====
[[Kell Douro]], an [[Anzat (species)|Anzati]] [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] who lived during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], claimed he could see what he called ''[[daen nosi]]'', a phrase from his [[Anzat (language)|species' language]] that meant "fate lines" in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], when he used his proboscises to consume the [[Soup (Anzati)|soup]], or [[Brain/Legends|brain]] matter, of another. Douro believed these lines crossed the universe and bound Fate together, a network of every sentient choice related to every other choice through knotting, and that by consuming the brains of Force sensitives he would be able to untangle them and completely understand Fate. Soup from some people was more potent than the soup from others, and consuming the former provided him with a clearer picture of how this network was woven.<ref name="Crosscurrent" />

In [[43 ABY]], Kell Douro became convinced that consuming the soup of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] named [[Jaden Korr]] would finally allow him to understand the ''daen nosi'' in full. He was [[Death/Legends|killed]] before he could do so.<ref name="Crosscurrent" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Now, for the first time, the facts, figures, and fascinating backstories of major clashes and combatants in the ''Star Wars'' universe have been documented in one fully-illustrated volume|The back cover of ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', referring to the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] and thereby events in ''the galaxy''|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />}}
Though certain usages of the word "universe" in the ''Star Wars'' galaxy could have been, in context, the character referring simply to the galaxy,<ref name="I novel" /><ref name="Anakin Journal" /> the existence of other galaxies connected by space meant a universe existed. Further, ''[[The Crystal Star]]'' established that there was a definitive difference between the space-time of the universe and Waru's universe, meaning that all things that have appeared in the standard ''Star Wars'' universe are relative to the ''Star Wars'' universe, even if the concept of the various galaxies being parts of a singular celestial association has never been extrapolated upon or spelled out flatly in a source.

Though most sources tend to just say "the universe" in reference to it, ''[[Boba Fett: The Fight to Survive]]'', a [[2002]] young-reader novel by [[Terry Bisson]], gave it a proper noun name as the "Known Universe." This terminology was also used in an earlier novel, ''[[Rogue Planet]]'' by [[Greg Bear]], but it was not treated as a proper noun. This phrase is used for our own universe because light has not yet traveled far enough for us to be able to see the entire universe. Because the universe is also expanding, the entire universe may never be observed.

It is common practice for people and the publishers of the stories to refer to the events in the ''Star Wars'' galaxy as events in the "''Star Wars'' universe,"<ref name="Karpa">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]'', Drew Karpyshyn's Acknowledgements.</ref> as the events in the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity outside the main six films are collectively called the Expanded Universe. Events in the stories are called ''[[in-universe]]'', and things outside them are called ''out-of-universe''.

The galaxy is said to be "far, far away" from our real galaxy, meaning that the universe is the same body as our real universe. Certain references have hinted at this. For instance, the [[Buick]], an [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter egg]] in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', was described as "a relic from a galaxy far, far away," when covering the origins and specs of the vehicle. As an easter egg, its [[canon]]icity is ambiguous.<ref name="RSIII">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>
